verses.1:1: James, a bondservant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes that are in the dispersion: Greetings.
verses.1:2: Regard it as all joy, my brethren, whenever you fall into diverse trials,
verses.1:3: knowing that the proving of your faith brings forth endurance.
verses.1:4: And let endurance have its complete work, so that you may be complete and whole, lacking in nothing.
verses.1:5: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask from God, who gives to all generously and without upbraiding, and it shall be given to him.
verses.1:6: Yet let him ask in faith, doubting nothing; for he who doubts resembles a billow of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed about.
verses.1:7: For that man must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord,
verses.1:8: being a double-minded man, unsteady in all his ways.
verses.1:9: Now let the lowly brother boast in his high estate,
verses.1:10: and the rich man in his humiliation, because like a flower of the grass he shall pass away.
verses.1:11: For the sun rises with its scorching heat and withers the grass, and its flower falls off, and the beauty of its appearance perishes; so also the rich man shall fade away in his endeavors.
verses.1:12: Blessed is the man who endures trial; for once he has been proved, he shall receive the crown of life, which He has promised to those who love Him.
verses.1:13: Let no one who is tempted say, "I am tempted from God"; for God cannot be tempted by evil things, and He Himself tempts no one.
verses.1:14: Rather, each one is tempted when he is drawn away and lured by his own desire;
verses.1:15: then desire, having conceived, bears sin; and sin, when it has reached its full measure, brings forth death.
verses.1:16: Do not be led astray, my beloved brethren.
verses.1:17: Every good bestowal and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no shifting nor shadow cast by turning.
verses.1:18: Of His own purpose He brought us forth by a word of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruits of His created works.
verses.1:19: Know this, my beloved brethren. And let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath,
verses.1:20: for the wrath of man does not accomplish the righteousness of God.
verses.1:21: Therefore, putting away all filthiness and abundance of wickedness, receive with meekness the implanted word, which has power to save your souls.
verses.1:22: And become doers of the word, and not hearers alone, deluding yourselves.
verses.1:23: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, such a one resembles a man beholding his natural countenance in a mirror;
verses.1:24: for he beholds himself and departs, and at once forgets what manner of man he was.
verses.1:25: But he who looks intently into the perfect law, that of liberty, and abides by it, proving not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work—this man shall be blessed in his doing.
verses.1:26: If anyone supposes himself to be religious, yet does not bridle his tongue, but deceives his own heart, this man's religion is vain.
verses.1:27: Religion pure and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained from the world.
verses.2:1: My brethren, do you hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of partiality?
verses.2:2: For if a man wearing a gold ring, in splendid apparel, enters your assembly, and a poor man in filthy garments also enters,
verses.2:3: and you pay special regard to the one wearing the splendid apparel and say, "Sit here in an honorable place," while to the poor man you say, "Stand over there," or, "Sit beneath my footstool,"
verses.2:4: have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil reasonings?
verses.2:5: Hear, my beloved brethren: did not God choose those who are poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom which He has promised to those who love Him?
verses.2:6: Yet you have dishonored the poor man. Are not the rich the ones who oppress you, and do they not themselves drag you into the courts?
verses.2:7: Do they not blaspheme the honorable name that has been invoked over you?
verses.2:8: If indeed you are fulfilling the royal law according to the Scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well;
verses.2:9: yet if you show partiality, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.
verses.2:10: For whoever keeps the entire law, yet stumbles in one point, has become guilty of all.
verses.2:11: For the One who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." So if you do not commit adultery, yet commit murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
verses.2:12: Thus speak and thus act, as those who are to be judged by the law of liberty.
verses.2:13: For judgment shall be merciless to the one who has shown no mercy; mercy exults over judgment.
verses.2:14: What is the profit, my brethren, if someone claims to have faith, yet has no works? Can that faith save him?
verses.2:15: If a brother or sister is naked and lacking in daily sustenance,
verses.2:16: and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be warmed and be filled," yet you do not give them the things needful for the body, what is the profit?
verses.2:17: In the same way faith also, if it has no works, is dead in itself.
verses.2:18: Yet someone will say, "You have faith, and I have works." Show me your faith apart from works, and I will show you faith by my works.
verses.2:19: You believe that God is one? You do well; even the demons believe, and shudder.
verses.2:20: Yet do you wish to learn, O empty man, that faith apart from works is barren?
verses.2:21: Was not our father Abraham justified by works when he offered up his son Isaac upon the altar?
verses.2:22: You see that faith was working alongside his works, and by works faith was brought to completion,
verses.2:23: and the Scripture was fulfilled which says, "And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness," and he was called the friend of God.
verses.2:24: You see that a man is justified by works, and not by faith alone.
verses.2:25: And in like manner, was not Rahab the harlot also justified by works, when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another way?
verses.2:26: For just as the body apart from the spirit is dead, so also faith apart from works is dead.
verses.3:1: Not many of you should become teachers, my brethren, knowing that we shall receive a weightier judgment.
verses.3:2: For we all stumble in many ways. If anyone does not stumble in word, this is a complete man, able to bridle the entire body as well.
verses.3:3: Now if we put bits into the mouths of horses so that they obey us, we also direct their entire body.
verses.3:4: Behold also the ships: though they are so great and are driven by fierce winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the helmsman wills.
verses.3:5: So also the tongue is a small member, yet it boasts of great things. Behold how small a fire kindles how vast a forest!
verses.3:6: And the tongue is a fire, the very world of iniquity. The tongue is set among our members, staining the entire body and setting ablaze the course of existence, and is itself set on fire by hell.
verses.3:7: For every species of wild beast and bird, of creeping thing and creature of the sea, is being tamed and has been tamed by mankind;
verses.3:8: yet no one among mankind is able to tame the tongue; it is a restless evil, full of deadly venom.
verses.3:9: With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse men who have been made in the likeness of God.
verses.3:10: From the same mouth come forth blessing and cursing; my brethren, these things should not happen thus.
verses.3:11: Does a spring gush forth fresh water and bitter from the same opening?
verses.3:12: Can a fig tree, my brethren, produce olives, or a vine produce figs? Neither can salt water yield fresh water.
verses.3:13: Who among you is wise and discerning? By his noble conduct let him show his works in the meekness of wisdom.
verses.3:14: Yet if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast and lie against the truth.
verses.3:15: Such wisdom is not that which comes down from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic;
verses.3:16: for where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is disorder and every vile practice.
verses.3:17: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, forbearing, readily yielding, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, and unfeigned.
verses.3:18: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace for those who make peace.
verses.4:1: From where do wars and from where do fights arise among you? Is it not from this—from your pleasures that wage war in your members?
verses.4:2: You crave, and you do not have; you murder and burn with envy, yet you are unable to obtain; you fight and wage war. You do not possess because you do not ask.
verses.4:3: You ask and do not receive, because you ask wickedly, that you may spend it upon your pleasures.
verses.4:4: You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity against God? Whoever, therefore, determines to be a friend of the world becomes an enemy of God.
verses.4:5: Or do you think that the Scripture speaks in vain, "With jealousy He longs for the spirit that He caused to dwell in us"?
verses.4:6: Yet He grants greater grace. Therefore it says, "God stands against the proud, but to the humble He gives grace."
verses.4:7: Be subject, therefore, to God; but withstand the devil, and he will flee from you.
verses.4:8: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, O sinners, and purify your hearts, O double-minded.
verses.4:9: Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep; let your laughter be transformed into mourning, and your joy into dejection.
verses.4:10: Humble yourselves in the presence of the Lord, and He will exalt you.
verses.4:11: Do not speak evil against one another, brethren. Whoever speaks evil against a brother or judges his brother speaks evil against the law and judges the law; yet if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law, but a judge.
verses.4:12: There is one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and to destroy; who then are you, who judge your neighbor?
verses.4:13: Come now, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will travel to such-and-such a city, spend a year there, engage in trade, and gain a profit,"
verses.4:14: whereas you do not know what tomorrow holds, or what your life is; for you are a vapor that appears for a short while and afterward vanishes away.
verses.4:15: Rather, you should say, "If the Lord wills, we shall both live and do this or that."
verses.4:16: As it is, however, you boast in your arrogant pretensions; all boasting of this kind is evil.
verses.4:17: Therefore, to the one who knows to do good and does not perform it, to him it is sin.
verses.5:1: Come now, you who are rich, weep with loud wailing over your miseries that are coming upon you.
verses.5:2: Your wealth has decayed, and your garments have become moth-eaten;
verses.5:3: your gold and your silver have corroded, and their corrosion shall stand as a witness against you and shall devour your flesh; as fire you have laid up treasure in the last days.
verses.5:4: Behold, the wages of the laborers who mowed your fields—kept back by you—cry aloud, and the cries of those who reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.
verses.5:5: You have dwelt in luxury upon the earth and indulged in excess; you have fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter.
verses.5:6: You have condemned, you have murdered the righteous one. Does he not resist you?
verses.5:7: Be patient, therefore, brethren, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the earth, waiting patiently over it until it receives the early and the late rain.
verses.5:8: Be patient, you also; make your hearts steadfast, for the coming of the Lord has drawn near.
verses.5:9: Do not groan against one another, brethren, lest you be judged; behold, the Judge stands before the doors.
verses.5:10: Take as an example of suffering hardship and of patience, brethren, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
verses.5:11: Behold, we call blessed those who endured. You have heard of the steadfast endurance of Job, and you have seen the purpose of the Lord—that the Lord is full of tender compassion and merciful.
verses.5:12: Above all things, however, my brethren, do not swear—neither by heaven, nor by earth, nor by any other oath; rather, let your "Yes" be yes and your "No" be no, lest you fall under judgment.
verses.5:13: Is anyone among you suffering hardship? Let him pray. Is anyone of good cheer? Let him sing praises.
verses.5:14: Is anyone among you sick? Let him summon the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.
verses.5:15: And the prayer of faith shall save the one who is ailing, and the Lord shall raise him up; and even if he has committed sins, he shall be forgiven.
verses.5:16: Confess your sins, therefore, to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The supplication of a righteous one avails greatly in its working.
verses.5:17: Elijah was a man of like nature with us, and he prayed fervently that it might not rain; and it did not rain upon the earth for three years and six months.
verses.5:18: And again he prayed, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
verses.5:19: My brethren, if anyone among you strays from the truth and someone turns him back,
verses.5:20: let him know that whoever turns a sinner back from the error of his way shall save his soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.

notes.1:12: The Greek critical text reads "which He has promised" with an implied divine subject, whereas later manuscripts supply "the Lord."
notes.1:17: The phrasing draws on astronomical imagery ("Father of lights," "shifting," "shadow cast by turning") to contrast the unchanging God with the changing heavenly bodies.
notes.1:19: Translates the critical text reading iste ("Know this") rather than the later variant hoste ("So then").
notes.1:25: The participle parakypsas literally means to stoop down and peer intently, emphasizing sustained attention to the law of liberty.
notes.2:1: Rendered as a question following the punctuation of the Greek source text, though the verb form echete may also be read as a prohibition ("Do not hold...").
notes.2:18: The extent of the speaker's quotation is debated; here it concludes after "and I have works," and the critical text reads "apart from works" rather than "by your works."
notes.2:20: Translates the critical text reading arge ("barren" or "idle") rather than the later variant nekra ("dead").
notes.2:23: Cites Genesis 15:6 according to the Septuagint wording.
notes.3:3: Translates the critical text reading ei de ("Now if") rather than the later variant idou ("Behold").
notes.3:6: "The course of existence" renders the rare Greek phrase ton trochon tes geneseos (literally "the wheel of birth/existence"), and "hell" translates geenna (Gehenna).
notes.3:8: Translates the critical text reading akatastaton ("restless" or "unstable") rather than the later variant akatascheton ("unruly").
notes.3:18: The Greek dative tois poiousin eirenen may be understood either as "for those who make peace" (dative of advantage) or "by those who make peace" (dative of agency).
notes.4:4: The Greek addresses the readers in the feminine plural (moichalides, "adulteresses"), evoking Old Testament imagery of covenant unfaithfulness to God; some later manuscripts expand this to "adulterers and adulteresses."
notes.4:5: The Greek syntax is famously debated and admits two main renderings: either God jealously longs for the human spirit He placed within us, or the Spirit whom He caused to dwell in us yearns with jealousy (following the critical verb katokisen, "caused to dwell").
notes.4:14: Following the Greek critical text, the second clause reads in the second person plural ("for you are a vapor") rather than the third person singular ("for it is a vapor") found in some later manuscripts.
notes.5:3: Following the punctuation of the Greek source text, the phrase "as fire" opens the final clause ("as fire you have laid up treasure"); other editions instead join it to the preceding clause ("shall devour your flesh like fire").
notes.5:4: "Sabaoth" is the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew word for "Hosts" or "Armies" (Kyriou Sabaoth, "Lord of Hosts").
notes.5:6: The Greek source text punctuates the final clause as a rhetorical question ("Does he not resist you?"); other editions punctuate it as a statement ("He does not resist you").
notes.5:20: Following the Greek critical text, the verse reads "his soul" (referring to the straying sinner's soul), whereas some manuscripts omit the possessive pronoun and read simply "a soul."
